chapterNote: The revival psalm — a prayer of the sons of Korah that moves through three tenses. Past: You were favorable to Your land, You brought back Jacob's captives, forgave their iniquity, covered their sin, withdrew Your wrath. Present: so turn us again, God of our salvation — will You be angry forever? will You not revive us again, that Your people may rejoice in You? It is the prayer of a people who know God has done it before and need Him to do it now. And then the psalmist stops talking and listens: 'I will hear what God the LORD will speak' — and what he hears is the future, one of the most beautiful visions in the Psalter. Covenant love and truth meet each other on the road; righteousness and peace kiss. Truth springs up from the earth while righteousness leans down from heaven; the LORD gives what is good, the land yields its harvest, and righteousness walks ahead of Him like a herald preparing the way for His footsteps. Christian readers have always seen Bethlehem in verse 11 — truth sprouting from the ground, righteousness looking down from heaven — and the cross in verse 10, where mercy and justice finally embraced.

1.text: For the choir director. A psalm of the sons of Korah. LORD, You showed favor to Your land; You brought back the captivity of Jacob.
1.amp: To the chief Musician [natsach], A Psalm [mizmor] for the sons of Korah [Qorach]. LORD [YHWH], You have been favourable ['well pleased', ratsah, the KJV margin] unto Your land [eretz]: You have brought back [shub] the captivity [shebut — the fortunes] of Jacob [Yaaqob].
1.notes: The psalm opens in the past tense, with the restoration-formula of Psalm 126: shub shebut (H7725, H7622), the turning of the captivity. ratsah (H7521) is delight — God took pleasure in His eretz again. Memory is the prayer's opening argument.

2.text: You lifted away the iniquity of Your people; You covered over all their sin. Selah.
2.amp: You have forgiven [nasa — lifted off, carried away] the iniquity [avon] of Your people [am], You have covered [kasah] all their sin [chattath]. Selah.
2.notes: The two forgiveness-verbs of Psalm 32:1, now in the plural: nasa avon and kasah chattath (H5375, H5771, H3680, H2403) — guilt lifted off the nation, sin covered by God's own hand. National revival began, as it always does, with pardon.

3.text: You gathered in all Your wrath; You turned back from the burning of Your anger.
3.amp: You have taken away [asaph — gathered in] all Your wrath [ebrah]: You have turned [shub] Yourself from the fierceness ['thine anger from waxing hot', charon, the KJV margin] of Your anger [aph].
3.notes: asaph (H622), the gathering-verb: wrath collected back like a spread net drawn in. And shub again — God Himself turning: the same verb that turned the captivity (v. 1) turned His charon aph (H2740, H639). The remembered mercies are now the template for the request.

4.text: Turn us back, O God of our salvation, and break off Your indignation toward us.
4.amp: Turn [shub] us, O God [Elohim] of our salvation [yesha], and cause Your anger [kaas — indignation] toward us to cease [parar — break, annul].
4.notes: The pivot to present tense, and the third shub in four verses: You turned the captivity, You turned from anger — now turn US. The people ask to be the object of the verb God has already proven He performs. parar (H6565): let the kaas be broken off like a broken treaty.

5.text: Will You be angry with us forever? Will You draw out Your anger through all generations?
5.amp: Will You be angry [anaph] with us for ever [olam]? will You draw out [mashak — prolong, drag on] Your anger [aph] to all generations [dor va-dor]?
5.notes: Lament's honest questions, asked by a people who know the answer from Psalm 30:5 — His anger is a moment — yet feel it dragging: mashak (H4900), anger pulled out long. The questions expect 'no'; they are a way of holding God to His own character.

6.text: Will You not turn and revive us again, so that Your people may rejoice in You?
6.amp: Will You not revive [chayah] us again [shub]: that Your people [am] may rejoice [samach] in You?
6.notes: The revival verse: chayah (H2421), the life-verb of Psalm 119, joined to shub — 'turn and make us live' — revival as God's returning to give life. The stated goal is not survival but samach BEKHA: a people glad in God Himself, which is what revival actually is.

7.text: Show us Your covenant love, O LORD, and grant us Your salvation.
7.amp: Show [raah — let us see] us Your mercy [chesed — covenant love], O LORD [YHWH], and grant [natan] us Your salvation [yesha].
7.notes: The petitions compress to two nouns: chesed and yesha (H2617, H3468), covenant love and rescue — raah, made visible, and natan, handed over. Verses 4-7 are the whole vocabulary of a praying church in four lines.

8.text: I will listen for what God the LORD will speak, for He will speak peace to His people, His faithful ones — but let them not turn back to folly.
8.amp: I will hear [shama] what God [El] the LORD [YHWH] will speak [dabar]: for He will speak peace [shalom] unto His people [am], and to His saints [chasid]: but let them not turn again [shub] to folly [kislah — self-confident foolishness].
8.notes: The psalm's hinge: the pray-er goes silent to shama. The answer's first word is shalom (H7965) to the chasidim — and its rider: the fourth shub of the psalm turned to warning, no return to kislah, the fool's confidence that caused the captivity. Revival received must not be revival squandered (cf. John 5:14).

9.text: Surely His salvation is near to those who fear Him, so that glory may dwell in our land.
9.amp: Surely His salvation [yesha] is nigh [qarov] them that fear [yare] Him; that glory [kabod] may dwell [shakan] in our land [eretz].
9.notes: qarov (H7138), near — the nearness-word of Psalm 145:18 applied to salvation itself. And the aim: kabod shakan (H3519, H7931), glory TABERNACLING in the eretz — the shekinah-verb: revival's end is God's presence resident again among His people (cf. Exodus 40:34; John 1:14).

10.text: Covenant love and truth have met one another; righteousness and peace have kissed.
10.amp: Mercy [chesed — covenant love] and truth [emeth] are met together [pagash — have encountered each other]; righteousness [tsedek] and peace [shalom] have kissed [nashaq] each other.
10.notes: One of Scripture's most beloved pictures: four attributes personified on the road — chesed and emeth (H2617, H571) pagash (H6298), meeting like travelers; tsedek and shalom (H6664, H7965) nashaq (H5401), kissing like reconciled kin. The church has always seen the cross here, where justice and mercy stopped opposing each other (cf. Romans 3:26).

11.text: Truth springs up from the earth, and righteousness leans down from heaven.
11.amp: Truth [emeth] shall spring out [tsamach — sprout, grow up] of the earth [eretz]; and righteousness [tsedek] shall look down [shaqaph — lean down and gaze] from heaven [shamayim].
11.notes: The vertical meeting: emeth tsamach (H6779) — the Branch-verb, the Messianic sprouting — from the eretz below, and tsedek shaqaph (H8259) from shamayim above. Read from Bethlehem it is an incarnation text: Truth grew up out of the ground of Judah while Righteousness bent down from heaven to meet it (cf. John 14:6; Isaiah 45:8).

12.text: Yes, the LORD Himself will give the good, and our land will give back its harvest.
12.amp: Yea, the LORD [YHWH] shall give [natan] that which is good [tov]; and our land [eretz] shall yield [natan] her increase [yebul].
12.notes: Two natan's: YHWH gives tov, and the land gives yebul (H2981) — the harvest-word of Psalm 67:6. Spiritual revival and literal fruitfulness in one verse; the covenant never separated the fields from the faith (cf. Leviticus 26:3-4).

13.text: Righteousness walks ahead of Him and prepares a road for His footsteps.
13.amp: Righteousness [tsedek] shall go [halak] before [panim] Him; and shall set [sum] us in the way [derek] of His steps [paam].
13.notes: tsedek as the King's herald, halak le-phanav — walking ahead to clear the derek for His peamim (H6471), His footfalls. The psalm ends with God on the move toward His people, righteousness laying the road; the Baptist would later be that herald in person (cf. Isaiah 40:3; Mark 1:2-3).
